plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms that unfurl against dark, leathery leaves. In mild winter gardens they bring rich color to the coldest weeks of the year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, with peak bloom from January through March in mild climates
plants.location: Japan, the southeastern United States and other mild temperate regions
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative of the Japanese camellia, is the plant that gives us tea.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A winter-flowering tree that opens fragrant blossoms on bare branches, sometimes while snow is still on the ground. Its sweet, spicy perfume drifts through gardens in the depths of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring, usually January through March
plants.location: China, Japan and Korea, including the plum groves of East Asia
plants.funFact: In East Asian culture the plum blossom stands for perseverance, because it blooms in the cold before the other trees.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall stems carry round clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers above arching, strap-like leaves. Each head looks like a small firework of blue.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly December through February
plants.location: Eastern South Africa, and gardens in Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Its name comes from the Greek words for love and flower, though it is not a true lily.
